title: Queued burst mitigator and SLA-preservation proxy for Dedicated fleets
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Tenant microbursts (short-lived spikes of concurrent requests) were causing Dedicated fleet autoscalers to overshoot scale-up decisions and to trigger aggressive scale-downs once the burst subsided, which in turn increased tail latencies and SLA violations for steady traffic. This PR introduces a lightweight per-fleet proxy (queued burst mitigator) that applies a token-bucket + queue admission policy at the fleet edge and exports a smoothed utilization proxy to the autoscaler. Goals: reduce scale oscillation, preserve per-tenant throughput SLAs during transient spikes, and provide actionable telemetry for SRE and the autoscaler.

What changed (high level):
- Add a new service component `fleet-burst-proxy` that sits in front of the existing request router for Dedicated fleets. It enforces short-window token buckets, a bounded request queue with backpressure signals, and fast local credit borrowing between sibling workers for short bursts.
- Implement a utilization_proxy aggregator that computes smoothed utilization metrics (EWMA, burst-adjusted) and exposes them via existing metrics and a new autoscaler ingestion endpoint.
- Autoscaler hook: read smoothed utilization instead of raw instantaneous utilization when making scale decisions; add a configurable burst_grace_period to avoid reacting to sub-second spikes.
- Add unit and integration tests that simulate microburst patterns and verify fewer scale actions and improved SLA preservation.
- Telemetry: new metrics prefixed fleet.burst.*, and new traces that annotate queue admission decisions.

Compatibility and rollout: the new proxy can be toggled via a feature flag per-cluster. Default rollout path is off for 24 hours, then gradual canary to 10% of fleets for a day, with automatic rollback if P95 latency increases by >15%.

Why this is different than previous approaches: prior PRs centered on smoothing the autoscaler signal alone. This PR intervenes earlier in the request path to clamp extreme short-lived demand and provide the autoscaler a more meaningful utilization signal so it can make stable decisions without sacrificing tenant SLAs.
